headlines.text: Asian stocks rocket higher as Japan's Nikkei tops 66,300 and South Korea's Kospi surges past 6,900, riding an AI-chip rally that spilled over from Friday's blowout U.S. jobs report.
U.S. payrolls smashed forecasts in August, adding 162,000 jobs as unemployment held at 4.1%, pushing Fed rate-hike odds for the Sept. 15-16 meeting to roughly 60%.
Trump, Vance and Bessent mount an unusually public campaign urging the Fed to cut rates, but Chair Kevin Warsh is signaling he may back a hike instead to keep fighting inflation.
All eyes turn to Friday's August CPI report, which Fed Governor Christopher Waller says will be "heavily influential" in deciding whether the Fed hikes or holds on Sept. 16.
Lululemon shares sank as much as 18% to an eight-year low after the retailer slashed its full-year guidance for the third time in 2026, citing a sharp slowdown in leggings sales.
Brent crude surged past $95 a barrel, up more than 8% on the week, after Iran and the U.S. traded attacks on oil tankers near the Strait of Hormuz.
U.S. stock markets are closed Monday for Labor Day, leaving Wall Street to digest the weekend's Hormuz tanker attacks and jobs-data fallout ahead of Tuesday's reopen.
